title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Monday, October 12th | Press Conference
headline: Michael Penix Jr. (rib) is questionable for the Bears game, with an update due Wednesday; C.J. Henderson (groin) is also being monitored.
summary: Stefanski said the Falcons were frustrated to lose a Sunday night game against Baltimore after failing to close it out despite leading by two scores in the second half. He said the team must learn from it and improve across offense, defense, special teams, players, and coaches. On injuries, he said Michael Penix Jr. has a rib injury and C.J. Henderson has a groin injury, with both being treated and monitored, and he will provide updates on Wednesday. Asked about Penix's availability for this week, he said it is probably a question he can answer better Wednesday. He credited Ravens QB Lamar Jackson's replacement, Snoop Huntley, and the Baltimore offense for their two-minute and overtime drives, and said the staff will review pass rush and fundamentals, especially against a strong run attack. On the offense, he said the team put itself in long third-down situations by failing on first and second down, forcing deep throws past the sticks. He praised Drake London as playing at an extremely high level. Cameron Thomas was chosen as the game captain by the leadership committee. Looking ahead, he called the Bears a well-coached team with talent throughout the roster and said the staff will start game-planning right away.

title: Dave Canales: 'There’s work to do'
headline: Tershawn Wharton and Taylor Moton's practice windows open this week, Jaelan Phillips has a chance to return, and Jalen Coker is on track; full injury updates come later in the week.
summary: Canales opened by describing the bye week as a time for coordinator meetings, self-scouting, and finding an edge, with the early bye arriving as some players battle back and others who have been out may see their windows open. He said the staff will open the practice window for Tershawn Wharton and Taylor Moton this week and will report how they respond, and that Wharton has been medically cleared but has not played football yet. Jaelan Phillips has a chance to play again, with details to come, and Canales praised his motor, size, and every-down run defense. Jalen Coker had a great bye, is on track, and has a couple of big practice days ahead, with a practice tomorrow to test his progress. Monroe Freeling is doing everything he can to be available despite a knee issue. On the offensive side, Canales said the team likes balancing under-center and gun/pistol runs, that a strong run game opens the passing game, and that Chuba Hubbard's conditioning and preparation are being managed carefully. On defense he credited Nick Scott's communication, Lathan Ransom's hits and open-field tackles, and Lee Hunter's growing comfort in the scheme. He framed the Philadelphia Eagles game as a championship opportunity and stressed a week-to-week focus rather than league-wide buzz.

title: Zac Taylor Discusses Week 5, Bye Week | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Zac Taylor flagged Tanner Hudson (pectoral) as a possible IR candidate and Kyle Dugger as week-to-week, while praising Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins' deep-ball usage and Jordan Battle's two interceptions heading into the Week 6 bye.
summary: Taylor said a player broke his forearm and will go to IR, and that Tanner Hudson has a pectoral issue still being evaluated. He said Kyle Dugger remains week to week, and these three are the main injury concerns coming out of the bye. He did not think the forearm injury was season-ending, but Hudson's status is still open. On offense, he credited the line and Joe Burrow's movement for the deep ball to Ja'Marr Chase, and he praised Drew Sample's blocking and his reliability as an outlet on play-action. Taylor said the run game worked, with backs running hard and gaining yards after contact, though he wants to fix the crack toss and reverse plays that produced explosive gains. He praised Jordan Battle's two takeaways and said the team's defensive coverage and pressure have been strong, though the team gave up too many points late and penalties remain a problem. He framed the bye as a chance to heal and rest before a divisional game at Baltimore, and he said the team's confidence in its deep-ball targets has paid off repeatedly.

title: HC Sean Payton on Denver’s Week 3 takeaways: ‘We win the game yesterday because of it’
headline: Payton says the offense has 'a ton of things' to fix before Thursday vs. Seattle, while defensive takeaways are driving wins.
summary: Payton said the biggest short-week challenges are time and proper recovery from the prior game, so each player's body is ready for a compressed schedule. Asked about J.K. Dobbins' heavy workload in Week 3, he said the team isn't taking polls and that the goal is to win games, without committing to a usage plan. He credited the defense's seven takeaways through five weeks, especially ball security, early punch-outs, and interceptions, for changing games and said the team still has things to clean up. He praised special teams returner-adjacent work and recent punting consistency in general terms. On Bo Nix, Payton said he and the quarterback will align on the plan each week, with some throws being aggressive and others smart. Asked about Nix's confidence, Payton declined to grade it on a Monday before a Thursday game. He said confidence comes from execution, and that after watching the film there are many offensive areas that are not going well and must improve. The team faces Seattle in a Thursday night game.

signals.note: Payton's candid critique of the offense suggests continued QB inconsistency and possible limits on aggressive downfield throws in a short week.

title: Campbell on playing complementary football
headline: Tom Kennedy is out for the season, leaving the punt return job open; Cade Mays is eyed for Week 7 and Keith Abney is growing at safety.
summary: Campbell called the Arizona win the most complete complementary game of the season, pointing to three-and-outs on five straight defensive drives, a strong special teams showing across all four units, and offensive plays by Sam LaPorta and Jared Goff that turned the game. He said the team wants to use the bye to decide what it really is, which players are making plays in critical moments, and what needs adjusting. On rookie Keith Abney, who moved from cornerback to safety in his first NFL start, he said there is meat on the bone and the team will keep developing him there. Tom Kennedy will have surgery and miss the season, and Devin White also needs surgery and will be out a while; the team has in-house punt return candidates and is looking outside, but does not want Amon-Ra St. Brown as a full-time returner. On the offensive line, Campbell said the group is trending up despite inconsistency, with Cade Mays ideally back around Week 7 but still needing to be evaluated at center. Blake Miller's knee brace is a minor aggravation, not a serious concern. The bye gives the team time to get some players back, and the run defense's bounce back was a team effort.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade & Texans vs. Jaguars
headline: David Montgomery is week to week with a groin injury, so Woody Marks should keep a larger early-down role, with a Jacksonville matchup next.
summary: Ryans said the team is excited about Marvin Harrison Jr., describing him as a productive playmaker whose prior relationship with C.J. Stroud from Ohio State should help him adjust, and he said Stroud was consulted during the process. Ryans credited Nick Caserio with completing the deal and framed it as adding as many good players as possible. He stressed that Harrison's physical is still pending, with a check later that afternoon, and that the focus is on 2026 rather than beyond. On David Montgomery, Ryans said the groin injury is week to week and that Woody Marks handled the load well Sunday with explosive runs, vision, and balance, and will see more work. Ryans praised Stroud's command and poise, and called Will Anderson the best defensive player on the team. He said penalties, especially holding, must be cleaned up. Kayden McDonald had a strong NFL debut on the interior line. Houston faces Jacksonville next, traveling Thursday after practice, and Ryans described the Jaguars as a physical, well-coached team.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 5 recap, Colts at Steelers
headline: Steichen praised Daniel Jones' poise and ball security and said Jonathan Taylor's usage will be scheme-driven, but the defense's tackling and takeaway problems remain unfixed heading into Week 6 at Tennessee.
summary: Steichen said the Week 5 loss was disappointing, citing a failed red-zone conversion attempt and two explosive touchdown plays allowed by the defense, a 50-yard and an 80-yard play. He said the team must keep working on tackling every day in practice and was encouraged that players such as Akeem Davis-Gaither and Sauce Gardner were taking accountability. He called Daniel Jones' performance solid, praising his pocket movement, accuracy, and calm play, and said the offense has been working to build chemistry with a receiver group that includes newer additions. On defense, he acknowledged the team is not where it needs to be in forcing turnovers and said players must attack the football more aggressively. He also said the team must play better on the road, where its record has been poor, and that the defense needs to win one-on-one matchups and scheme better against quick passing games. Steichen described culture as daily behavior and preparation, and said Jones' late-game dip in completion percentage came from being down two scores and throwing more aggressively.

title: Andy Reid Speaks to the Media | Press Conference 10/12
headline: Tyquan Thornton likely heads to IR, so Xavier Worthy and Cyrus Allen should see more downfield work, while Kingsley Suamataia is expected back this week.
summary: Reid opened by noting this was a coaches-only day with no player injury updates, but said Tyquan Thornton is most likely going on IR and that the team is elevating a player and signing Justin Watson to the practice squad. He said the team self-scouted during the bye and identified short-yardage stops as the clearest area to fix, along with many smaller details. On the passing game, he expected Xavier Worthy to remain a major target and said the other receivers, who all have speed, would mix in to replace Thornton's deep-field role. He said Cyrus Allen would likely get more involved as he develops, similar to the progression Rashee Rice showed as a rookie. Reid said the offense is scoring and has a good mix, and described this week's opponent's defense as good despite their record. He said Kingsley Suamataia, who sat out last week, will be back, and that the team has generated pressure on the quarterback even without recent sacks. Reid said Kenneth Walker III has not surprised him, since the team saw his full skill set during the playoffs.

title: Jim Harbaugh on the Team's Determination to Improve and Win
headline: Harbaugh says Ladd McConkey could work back into practice this week, Quentin Johnston will be limited, and Tarheeb Still is week to week with a hamstring injury.
summary: Harbaugh said he still regrets the two fourth-down decisions, especially the one, and apologized for them because he believes he was wrong. He said Ladd McConkey played in an emergency situation the team did not want to put him in, and that McConkey is hopefully back in some capacity this week, though the coach was unsure. McConkey has not practiced for a few weeks and is rehabbing. Harbaugh said Trey's status and the hamstring situations are day to day or week to week, and he described the wide receiver room as competing hard. He praised the rookie offensive linemen, three of whom made their first career starts, saying they did well in protection and the run game apart from a few lapses late. On Justin Herbert, he said the quarterback is 'hell bent' on winning and sometimes forces plays in desperation, but he would not tell him to change his competitive style. Harbaugh said the team is determined to turn the season around, drawing confidence from players and coaches, and said ownership is united with the team. He defended his two challenges, saying the first was a knee-down question he wanted reviewed and the second was a possible tipped pass that was worth challenging. He also said the team must improve complementary football, starting with turnovers, and praised several defenders' play.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 12, 2026
headline: Sirianni is hopeful Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith return soon, and RB Dameon Pierce is the clear next-man-up back after Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley were hurt in the Jacksonville loss.
summary: Sirianni said the offense has to get better across the board and that the staff is focused on growth rather than grading individual players. He framed the late-game sequence against Jacksonville as a team practice issue: the staff rehearses two-minute situations every Wednesday, and he took responsibility for the decision that gave the ball back with eight seconds left. He said Jalen Hurts executes the calls the staff sends in, so he isn't asked to make late-game play decisions. On the injuries, he said the team won't use them as an excuse and that the answer is finding solutions. He is hopeful that Barkley and Smith return, but he won't commit until the end of the week. He said the running back group was strong heading into the season, singled out Pierce's runs and pass protection, praised Carson Steele, said Jaydon Blue has worked hard, and was pleased with Elijah Mitchell. He described the 2-3 start as early, with no panic in the building.

title: Kyle Shanahan: ‘We Have a Bunch of Warriors on This Team’
headline: Shanahan calls the Seattle win a gritty team effort; Renardo Green's two picks and Brock Purdy's fourth-quarter play stand out, with Greenlaw's injury and a hamstring question still open.
summary: Shanahan said the win over Seattle was a hard-fought, emotional game with many turnovers and momentum swings, and that the team's grit across all three phases carried it. He credited Mike Evans for making the key plays on the long touchdown drive, which he said was exactly why the team acquired him. He praised the defense for forcing four turnovers that decided the game, limiting explosive plays, and holding up against the run despite losing Dre Greenlaw early. He singled out Renardo Green (transcribed as 'Bernardo') for two interceptions, a key stop on a slant near the end, and smart play while playing through flu-like symptoms. Shanahan said Brock Purdy did an unbelievable job finding a way to win, especially in the fourth quarter, though not everything was perfect. He praised the offensive line for giving Purdy time and blocking well in the run game, and called the punter unbelievable in the field-position battle. On a sideline ejection, he said he hadn't fully seen it, but if a player headbutted an opponent without a helmet, he needs to be smarter. He said the team is only thinking about this game and will see Seattle at least one more time. He also said Mykel Williams was playing his first game back and Jaden Dugger stepped up in base and nickel. Shanahan said Jacob Cowing and Khalid Kareem had ankle and stinger issues that have returned to play, and that he has no update on the hamstring injury yet and expects to share one tomorrow.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 10/12/26
headline: No clear fantasy usage change; Stefon Diggs and Nick Cross injury updates come Thursday, with the team playing at San Francisco Monday night.
summary: Quinn said he was furious with the team's execution in the final moments of the overtime loss, especially the clock management on the last drive. He said the failure was in substitutions, clock awareness, and clocking the ball, not in the play call itself, and that the team spent its meeting time on how and why it broke down. He took responsibility for the communication framework, saying the process starts with him and that the play caller relays the calls. He said he still trusts the locker room and that he and ownership talk regularly after games, including hard conversations about what needs fixing. On defense, he said the group was mostly solid but gave up touchdowns in the middle of the third and fourth quarters, and he wants to close games better. He also said the team had three pre-snap false starts and will keep working on cadence and discipline with an extra official on the line. On injuries, he said he is encouraged by medical reports on Stefon Diggs and Nick Cross, with a fuller update coming Thursday, and that Javontae Jean-Baptiste hurt his back, though the team is still gathering information. Quinn also said the R&D work was split into a replay/officiating role and a game management/analytics role.
